usage.title: How may Home Assistant use the Multi?
usage.description:
- **Monitor only:** Home Assistant reads values and never changes how the Multi operates.
- **Monitor and control:** Home Assistant can also change how the Multi operates: controls on the dashboard and guided device actions.

You can change this later with *Reconfigure*.

control_warning.title: ⚠️ Read this before enabling control
control_warning.description:
**DO NOT CHANGE ANY SETTING IF YOU ARE NOT SURE WHAT IT DOES.**

Wrong settings can cut the power on AC out 1 and AC out 2, stop the battery from charging, or damage the battery, the Multi and connected equipment.

- Critical changes (mode, stopping grid charging, restart, charge voltages, PowerAssist, UPS function, equalisation, saving settings permanently) are locked. They work after turning on *Allow critical changes* on the device page (it turns itself off again after 10 minutes), in the guided *Configure → Device actions* dialog, or in actions with `acknowledge_risk: true`. Each shows its risks.
- Restarting the Multi, or switching its relays, cuts the power on AC out 1 and AC out 2: **every device connected to them is switched off and on again (power cycled).**
- By default settings change in the Multi's RAM only and return to the stored configuration when it restarts.

**Disclaimer:** this is an unofficial community integration. It is not made, endorsed or supported by Victron Energy. It is provided as is, without any warranty. The authors and contributors take **no responsibility whatsoever** for any damage to equipment, batteries or property, for injury, or for any other loss caused by using it. You use it entirely at your own risk.

disable_battery_limits.title: Turn off battery operational limits
disable_battery_limits.description:
Monitoring only switches battery operational limits off. The Multi keeps expecting them until it restarts: **it stops charging and inverting 5 minutes after Home Assistant stops sending them**. Restart the Multi (switch it off and on) within 5 minutes after confirming, or keep *Monitor and control*.

**A restart power cycles every device connected to AC out 1 and AC out 2.**

disable_battery_limits.title: Turn off battery operational limits
disable_battery_limits.description:
The Multi keeps expecting battery limits until it restarts. Once Home Assistant stops sending them, **the Multi stops charging and inverting after 5 minutes**. Restart the Multi (switch it off and on) within 5 minutes after confirming, or leave this option on.

**A restart power cycles every device connected to AC out 1 and AC out 2.** Turn this option off only at a moment when that is acceptable.

menu_options.actions: Device actions (restart, mode, grid charging, charger settings…)

data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls. At 2400 baud one poll takes about a second.
data_description.alarm_issues: Raise a repair issue while the Multi reports an overload, low battery or temperature alarm. Warnings (pre-alarms) and alarms are always available as events of the Alarm entity.
data_description.enable_battery_limits: Advanced, lithium batteries only. Creates four numbers whose limits are sent to the Multi on every poll, like a battery management system. WARNING: once the Multi has received limits, it stops charging AND inverting if it gets none for 5 minutes, and keeps expecting them until it is restarted (a restart power cycles AC out 1 and AC out 2). Needs device firmware 415 or later.
data_description.enable_ess_control: Only with the ESS assistant. Creates the switch and setpoint numbers that let Home Assistant control how much power is taken from or fed into the grid. Not verified on hardware: the sign of the setpoint and what the Multi does when the setpoint stops being refreshed are untested. Control always starts off and is handed back (0 W) when Home Assistant stops.

action_passthru.title: Stop grid charging
action_passthru.description:
Sets the remote AC input current limit to 0 A: the charger stops and the grid is passed straight through to the AC outputs (Victron calls this passthru). Normal operation (mode on) does not need it. To resume, the limit below is restored. It must be within the range the Multi reports.

enable_experimental.title: Enable an experimental function
enable_experimental.description:
Battery operational limits and ESS external control have only been tested against a simulator, not on a real Multi.

- **Battery limits:** once the Multi has received them, it **stops charging AND inverting** if they don't arrive for 5 minutes, until it is restarted. A wrong charge voltage can overcharge the battery. Lithium batteries with a BMS only, never lead.
- **ESS control:** a wrong sign turns import into export. If Home Assistant crashes, the last setpoint may stay in effect until the ESS assistant's own timeout.

Use them only if you understand these risks and can supervise the system.

device_unreachable.title: VE.Bus device unreachable
device_unreachable.description:
The VE.Bus device on {device} has not responded for more than 5 minutes ({error}).

If the device was switched off it may have gone to sleep, which also cuts the power of the MK3 interface. Switch it on at the device, and keep the "Keep awake" switch on to prevent this. Also check the cable between the MK3 and the device.

overload_alarm.title: {name}: overload alarm
overload_alarm.description:
The Multi reports an **overload alarm**: the loads on its AC outputs draw more power than it can supply.

Reduce the load. A Multi that stays overloaded switches off and tries to restart, so **AC out 1 and AC out 2 can lose power**.

This message disappears by itself when the alarm clears. To stop these messages, turn off *Show alarms as repair issues* in the integration settings.

low_battery_alarm.title: {name}: low battery alarm
low_battery_alarm.description:
The Multi reports a **low battery alarm**: the battery voltage has fallen below the shutdown voltage, so the inverter switches off. **The AC outputs lose power** unless the AC input is connected.

The inverter starts again when the battery has been charged above the restart voltage. Check the battery, its state of charge and the charge sources.

This message disappears by itself when the alarm clears. To stop these messages, turn off *Show alarms as repair issues* in the integration settings.

temperature_alarm.title: {name}: high temperature alarm
temperature_alarm.description:
The Multi reports a **high temperature alarm** and switches off to protect itself, so **AC out 1 and AC out 2 can lose power**.

Check the ventilation around the Multi, its fans and the ambient temperature, and reduce the load or charge current. (With a battery temperature sensor this alarm can also mean that the battery is too hot or too cold.)

This message disappears by itself when the alarm clears. To stop these messages, turn off *Show alarms as repair issues* in the integration settings.

ripple_alarm.title: {name}: high DC ripple alarm
ripple_alarm.description:
The Multi reports a **ripple alarm**: the battery voltage ripples too much under load. After repeated ripple alarms the Multi switches off, so **AC out 1 and AC out 2 can lose power**.

Check the battery cables (too long or too thin) and their connections (loose or corroded), the battery fuse, and whether the battery is too small or worn for the load or charge current. The *Battery ripple voltage* sensor shows the ripple.

This message disappears by itself when the alarm clears. To stop these messages, turn off *Show alarms as repair issues* in the integration settings.

vebus_error_alarm.title: {name}: VE.Bus error {code}
vebus_error_alarm.description:
The Multi reports **VE.Bus error {code}**. A VE.Bus error usually means the system can't run normally: the Multi may switch off, so **AC out 1 and AC out 2 can lose power**.

Look up error {code} in Victron's list of VE.Bus error codes (search for "VE.Bus error codes" on victronenergy.com) for its cause and what to check. The integration reads this code as VictronConnect does; Victron doesn't document how it is sent.

This message disappears by itself when the error clears. To stop these messages, turn off *Show alarms as repair issues* in the integration settings.

poor_link.title: {name}: poor connection to the VE.Bus device

battery_limits_stale.title: {name}: battery limits are not getting through
battery_limits_stale.description:
Home Assistant hasn't been able to send the battery operational limits to the Multi for more than 2 minutes. **If none arrive for 5 minutes, the Multi stops charging AND inverting** until it is restarted, and the AC outputs lose power when there is no grid.

Check the connection to the MK3 and the Multi. This message disappears by itself once limits are sent again.
